de.sch1.title:
Driver (stage 2): IR2110 half-bridge.  * 10 Ω gate resistors; ~1 µs dead time set by the
74HC14 shaper (RC+1N4148 at its inputs) — verify on a scope before applying power
de.sch1.vcc: +12 V (gate drive; 100 nF ∥ 47 µF at the pin)
de.sch1.vdd: +3.3 V (shared with AD9833; 100 nF at the pin)
de.sch2.title:
Receiver (stage 1): rectifier for the sweep map. An open piezo at resonance puts out
tens to hundreds of volts — fit the TVS BEFORE first power-up (docs/02)
de.sch3.title: Stage 1 wiring (sweep): raspi-config → enable SPI and I2C; run sweep_map.py
de.sch4.note:
bridge built into LTC3588-1;
VOUT jumpers → 3.3 V
de.sch4.title: Node (stage 4): harvester. The LTC3588-1 rectifies on its own (PZ1/PZ2); the supercap buffers BLE peaks

de.sim0.footer: 001: sweep 25–45 kHz → pair resonance → 002: half-bridge + watts (model sketch, not lab data)
de.sim1.note:
pair resonance ≈ 40.1 kHz,
peak width ~1 kHz if Q~40 (assumed)
de.sim1.title: Stage 1 expectation: channel sweep map (model, 3 mm steel, Langevin pair)
de.sim2.note:
takeaway: buy Langevins from one batch
and always start with a sweep; watts are targets until exp. 002
de.sim2.title: Model: pair Δf dominates power (10 W drive, η≤40% assumed, Q~40)
de.sim3.note: peaks every v/2d: 3 mm → 0.98 MHz; a 6% shift drops transmission ~10× → frequency auto-tracking required (docs/03)
de.sim3.title: Mode B: the plate is most transparent at thickness resonances
de.sim4.title: Receiver budget vs target bands (not measured — stage 2+ goals)
de.sim5.note.fast: ring-down eats the edges: the eye closes — faster is mode B territory
de.sim5.note.slow: τ ≪ bit period: clean edges, a 0.5 threshold tells 0/1 apart — stage 3 is real
de.sim5.title: Stage 3: data = keying the carrier on/off; resonator ring-down (Q~{q}) gives τ≈{tau} ms
